title: Orphans
summary: Mages who Awaken alone, with no Tradition to teach them.

claims.text: Self-taught Awakenings happen at any age but most often in the teens and early adulthood, when stress and new experience pile up.
Some orphans burn out in fire or madness; others end up homeless, jailed or committed because the world has no place for them.

title: Darklings in the occult revival
summary: How the Hollow Ones' forebears moved through the old occult societies.

claims.text: Darklings joined many occult societies in Britain, New England, France and Germany, rubbing shoulders with figures such as Crowley, Levi and Mathers, yet swore loyalty to no sect.
When the Order of Reason became the Technocratic Union in the mid-1800s, several were caught in the fighting, and the survivors passed on a warning to stay out of wizards' affairs.

title: The Unseen Society
summary: A Darkling fellowship of equals founded at Hazelton manor.

claims.text: Gladys and Gardner founded the Society at Hazelton as a modern druids' grove where Darklings could meet without bowing to anyone; many small sects copied it.
Hazelton later vanished from sight, moved or hidden by enchantment; it still appears now and then to wanderers or self-Awakened mages in need, but cannot be found by searching.
Gladys was killed by the Countessa d'Marque during the Second World War.

title: The Hollow Ones' status game
summary: How Darklings judge one another by style.

claims.text: A cliquish circle may test a newcomer without warning; style counts as much as power.
Los Angeles has two rival queens, Madelyne and Lady Zee, who both expect flashy displays; the Unseen Society prizes wicked wit and frowns on tacky magick.

title: Chapel Perilous
summary: A Hollow One nightclub in a burned-out neighbourhood.

claims.text: The club takes up a vast former Catholic church, no longer consecrated, set between two burned-out apartment blocks, lit by black lights and draped with real giant spiderwebs.
It is known as the easiest place in the city to buy drugs, and the decaying Victorian streets around it are full of the scene's young.

title: Strange
summary: Front man of the 1970s band Strange Therapy.

claims.text: Strange Therapy mixed glam and early punk with electric violin, and its singer, known only as Strange, wrote every song.
Before the recorded launch show of the second tour, Strange suffered crippling headaches and waking nightmares.
